note: Machine-readable copy of section 2. verdict values: sound | sound-with-correction | reframe.

verdict.sound: Holds up as stated as a developer requirement.
verdict.sound-with-correction: Holds up, but one premise in the ask is wrong and changes what you get.
verdict.reframe: The underlying goal is right, the framing leads somewhere unhelpful.

asks.ask: Weigh the Composio layer against Bubble
asks.why: The comparison assumes overlapping scope. 1,069 toolkits carry zero databases, warehouses or object stores, so the real question is where the seam sits.
asks.composio: SaaS breadth and a credential vault. 40 of 53 BubbleLab third-party integrations already exist, with 1x to 26x more operations each.
asks.bubblelab: The execution substrate: parser, type system, credential model, canvas, studio. Composio has no equivalent.
asks.merge: Composio underneath as credential and transport, BubbleLab on top as the product surface.

asks.ask: Get Bubble's structure with Composio's toolset and managed auth
asks.why: Managed auth covers 122 of 1,069 toolkits. 915 need the user's own OAuth app or API key. 45 are OAuth-only with no managed app and no key fallback, including twitter, xero, docusign, snowflake.
asks.composio: OAuth refresh, token storage, revocation, per-user connection scoping, restrict_to_following_tools for server-enforced tool limits.
asks.bubblelab: 68 CredentialType members, per-step binding, credential pools, SYSTEM_CREDENTIALS set. All hand-maintained.
asks.merge: Replace credential storage and refresh, keep the credential model. Bind a step to a connectedAccountId rather than a secret.

asks.ask: Is what Composio serves identical to the vendor's actual API?
asks.why: Decisive question for developer experience. Version management is beside the point: the SDK resolves to the newest surface by default.
asks.composio: Surface trails the vendor by a release cycle, and the trailing is mostly benign. Tracked Notion 2025-09-03 data sources and Slack's files.upload retirement (sunset date documented in the schema). Holds a Notion-Version 2025-09-03 pin rather than tracking 2026-03-11 (after -> position, archived -> in_trash). Coverage against Notion's own endpoint index: 25 of 28 (89%). No field reports which vendor changes landed.
asks.bubblelab: Every bubble hand-written, so coverage and currency are both your team's cost across 53 integrations (61 service bubbles, 536 operations). Hand-authoring is not faster at tracking a vendor's breaking change.
asks.merge: Composio absorbs maintenance for the 40 overlapping integrations, nothing for the 13 it lacks. Gate per toolkit on the vendor's versioning model rather than globally.

class_A_version_pinned.notion: No plans to stop supporting older API versions (stated policy). No version retired to date.
class_A_version_pinned.github: Dated versions; previous version supported at least 24 months after its successor; sunset returns 410. Removals confined to fields deprecated for years (has_downloads 10+ years, authorizations_url since 2020).
class_A_version_pinned.verdict: Provider drift is close to theoretical. No ongoing vigilance needed.

class_B_global_retirement.slack: files.upload retired outright (sunset 2025-11-12), legacy custom bots discontinued 2025-03-31, classic apps sunset 2026-11-16. Six breaking changes 2024-2026, mostly actual removals.
class_B_global_retirement.google: Turns APIs down rather than versioning: Email Settings API off 2017, Apps Script Contacts service off 2025-01-31.
class_B_global_retirement.verdict: Drift is real and has already materialised once. Watch the vendor changelog and execute one live call per tool before shipping.

drift_base_rates.synthesis: Composio migrates when a vendor removes things and pins when the vendor keeps old versions alive. Both responses are correct, so the trail reflects vendor policy rather than Composio neglect.

asks.ask: Re-test the logged complaints and gauge UX and DX damage
asks.why: Logged complaints are the cheapest available signal on adoption risk.
asks.composio: Two of three confirmed. Callback-URI contradiction: MEDIUM, costs one line of defensive code. Hidden github PAT: LOW, skip it since github has managed OAuth so the frictionless path is already default and users reach for OAuth anyway.
asks.bubblelab: Not applicable. The third complaint traced to Gluu's own connect flow.
asks.merge: The pattern outranks any single complaint: metadata under-reports what execution accepts, across auth schemes, tool counts, callback URIs and vendor currency. Verify by executing rather than by reading the catalog.

severity.complaint_2_setup_sequencing: medium, and it is Gluu's to fix
severity.complaint_3_hidden_pat: low, deprioritised on the user's call

asks.composio: Data path (every payload transits Composio, self-host is Enterprise-only), per-call billing, added hop, widened failure surface, thin triggers (351 across 1,069 toolkits), credential lock-in.
asks.bubblelab: Hybrid flows keep the AST injector in charge of bubbles, so both failure modes persist until bubbles migrate too.
asks.merge: Data path and per-call billing are the two most likely to change the answer.

asks.ask: Wrap Composio tools inside BubbleLab's type enforcement
asks.why: Highest-value ask in the brief and the one the evidence supports most cleanly.
asks.composio: 100% of sampled tools publish full JSON Schema for inputs and outputs using $defs and $ref. The SDK then discards it: ToolExecuteResponse.data is Record<string, unknown>.
asks.bubblelab: Zod-validated parameters, compile-time checks, typed errors.
asks.merge: Generate Zod plus TypeScript per tool per pinned version, parse at the boundary, reject is_deprecated slugs at generation time.

asks.ask: AST-detect Composio modules to fix the nested-credential bug
asks.why: Under Composio the problem stops existing, because credentials never enter the script. AST detection becomes a display mechanism rather than a correctness mechanism.
asks.composio: Dissolves the bug. A call inside a ternary, a .map(), or an agent-chosen tool all behave the same.
asks.bubblelab: Bug is structural and live. BubbleParser skips instantiation sites inside ConditionalExpression, ObjectExpression, ArrayExpression, Property and SpreadElement (BubbleParser.ts:1384-1394). Nested tool credentials come from string-parsing the tools parameter with new Function, failing to console.debug plus an empty array.
asks.merge: Reading a string literal off a call expression needs no call-site whitelist. Limits: dynamic slugs and provider handoff resolve to unknown, so static analysis is a predicted overlay, never the record of truth.

asks.ask: Sandbox fills credentials at runtime, clients declared at the top of the script
asks.why: Right instinct, and Composio's version is stronger. Your model still puts the credential in the process and still needs routing logic.
asks.composio: Removes the credential from the process entirely. Resolution happens server-side from (userId, toolkit).
asks.bubblelab: Current AST-rewriting model. Fails silently on unrecognised call sites and on nested tools.
asks.merge: Composio wins outright. Keep one requirement either way: a missing credential must throw at client construction, since a missing connected account surfaces only as successful:false at execution.

asks.ask: Join credential records to the tools that use them, and show it to the user
asks.why: The ask that most needs runtime truth rather than static analysis.
asks.composio: logId on every execute response and connectedAccountId as both input parameter and queryable entity. The join key is handed to you.
asks.bubblelab: Per-invocation variableId clones, the right granularity, sourced from static parsing that can miss.
asks.merge: Static AST pass populates a predicted checklist at save time, the execution wrapper writes authoritative rows, reconciliation exposes tools the agent chose but the flow never declared.

asks.ask: Keep the experiment read-only with tests in their own folder
asks.composio: One external write disclosed: an auth config created and deleted to settle Complaint 3.
asks.bubblelab: No BubbleLab or Gluu file modified.

asks.ask: Parseable enough to render visually for non-technical people
asks.why: Underrated in the brief. Cleanest complementary split in the comparison, since each platform holds the half the other lacks.
asks.composio: Labels. 209/209 tools carry prose names with zero slug-like values, 209/209 carry descriptions, 115/209 carry human_description, 1,069/1,069 toolkits carry a logo plus one of 88 categories. Behavioural tags include destructiveHint, readOnlyHint, idempotentHint, createHint, updateHint and important. No flow structure of any kind.
asks.bubblelab: Structure. ParsedBubble carries variableName, className, parameters, hasAwait, dependencies, dependencyGraph, invocationCallSiteKey and line numbers, plus the injected invocation dependency map. Labels exist per integration (53) rather than per operation.
asks.merge: BubbleLab's parser supplies the graph, Composio supplies node labels, logos, categories and risk badges. Render from reconciled A9 data rather than static parsing alone, and treat destructiveHint as a first-class UI signal.
asks.caveat: scopes is inconsistent and cannot drive a permissions display alone: notion returns human labels (18/56 populated), slack returns scope strings (93/100), googlesheets returns raw Google URLs (53/53). A mapping table is required.
